note: Art direction for Hui Hai (HH1), chosen by the owner on 2026-09-27: the Hàng Trống folk painting 'White Tiger' (Bạch hổ), Hanoi, traditional design (public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:White_tiger_Hang_Trong.jpg). The owner's bar: a real hand-made painting in the tiger's own bright, saturated gouache-and-watercolour look, never cute game art. The Hui Hai are drawn as tiny spirit folk in leaf clothes, never as a picture of the Ba Na people.
style: A painting in EXACTLY the look of the reference image, the Vietnamese Hàng Trống folk painting of the White Tiger: the same luminous, vibrant, highly saturated colours and the same brightness. Hand-painted with opaque gouache and watercolour on paper: a clean, flat, bright cobalt-blue ground; big bold simple shapes; the main figure large in the picture, painted in glowing cream-white and pale pink with hot-pink and vermilion outlines, exactly like the tiger's white fur with its pink edges; fur, hair, leaves and grass drawn with loose, fine parallel brush strokes in olive and grey, like the tiger's stripes; swirling cloud scrolls in hot pink, emerald green, orange and lemon yellow with white edges along the top; bright orange-ochre rocks below; accents of pure vermilion red and leaf green. Few elements, lots of flat bright colour, cheerful and naive, soft slightly blurred watercolour edges. Keep it BRIGHT and LIGHT like the reference: no dark shadows, no murky or muddy colours, no busy detailed backgrounds, no dense undergrowth. Faces are stylised the way the reference stylises the tiger's face: a few simple painted lines, not realistic and not cartoon-cute. Do not draw a tiger or a cat and do not copy its composition. The Hui Hai are tiny forest spirits of Vietnam's Central Highlands, drawn close up so the figure fills much of the picture, with fern leaves and pebbles shown huge beside them to tell their small size; they wear clothes of woven leaves and fern fronds; never a picture of any real people or their dress. A real hand-made painting, not digital illustration, not a cartoon, not anime, no big eyes, no glossy or 3D rendering. Absolutely no text, letters, Chinese characters, seals, stamps or watermarks. Match the reference's colour exactly: soft, chalky, slightly powdery opaque gouache, bright but not neon, with LARGE areas of cream white and pale pink (the main figure, its clothes and the big leaves are pale and light, like the tiger's white body), greens kept soft and sparing, the paint thin and matte with soft slightly blurred edges, like an old printed reproduction of the painting. Rocks are flat ochre-orange shapes with a few dark brown patches and no 3D shading or highlights. No thick impasto. The blue ground is a mid cerulean-cobalt, a little lighter and slightly mottled with uneven brushing like the reference, not a deep, even royal blue. Rocks are rough orange-ochre shapes blotched with dark brown patches and outlined, as under the tiger's feet, with no smooth shading or highlights. Faces are simple folk-painting faces drawn with a few lines.

families.Hui Hai: Background: the flat bright cobalt-blue ground and the many-coloured cloud scrolls of the reference, with a red sun, one or two huge pale fern fronds, a stem of bamboo and a few flat ochre pebbles.

subjects.HH1-H01-kitten: the littlest Hui Hai: a tiny girl spirit in a pale cream dress woven of dry leaves, her white-and-grey hair in a tuft tied with a grass blade, pushing with both arms a rough ochre boulder many times her size, beside one huge pale fern frond. Her face is an old Vietnamese folk-painting face like a Đông Hồ or Hàng Trống child: a round flat face, two small almond eyes drawn as short ink strokes, arched thin brows, a tiny red mouth, pink cheek dabs; no eyelashes, no manga or anime eyes, no smirk, a calm, simple expression.
subjects.HH1-H01-bigcat: the littlest Hui Hai: a tiny girl spirit in a pale cream dress woven of dry leaves, standing proudly on top of a rough ochre boulder in a stream, holding a pebble high over her head in one hand, the stream drawn as bands of white and pale blue wave lines around the boulder, one huge pale fern frond bowing over her. Her face is an old Vietnamese folk-painting face like a Đông Hồ or Hàng Trống child: a round flat face, two small almond eyes drawn as short ink strokes, arched thin brows, a tiny red mouth, pink cheek dabs; no eyelashes, no manga or anime eyes, no smirk, a calm, simple expression.
subjects.HH1-D01: a Hui Hai of the stream: a tiny boy spirit in a pale cream cape of fern fronds crouched on a rough ochre rock in a stream drawn as bands of white and pale blue wave lines, flicking a splash of water at a small pink-and-orange fish.
subjects.HH1-D02: Yă Hui Hai, Lady of the Ferns: a tiny old woman spirit with white hair in a bun and a calm face, wrapped in a pale cream shawl woven of dry fern and moss, sitting in the coil of one huge pale-green unfurling fern frond, one hand resting on a big flat ochre rock beside her.
subjects.HH1-D03: no full figure: a single round pebble landing with a little white splash of dust beside a big pair of plain woven straw sandals on rough ochre ground; at the side one huge pale fern frond, and in a gap between its leaflets two tiny round eyes of an unseen little spirit, clearly eyes in a shadowy gap of the leaves, not birds, no face or body shown.
